name: Project Management Checklist
description: A methodical checklist that walks a project through all five management phases.

items.text: Define the business case and the problem the project solves
Identify the sponsor and confirm executive support
Draft a project charter with goals and high-level scope
Map the key stakeholders and their interests
Get formal approval to proceed before any planning starts
items.note: Written authorization protects the project later.

items.text: Break the scope into a work breakdown structure
Build a schedule with milestones and dependencies
Estimate the budget and confirm funding
Define roles with a responsibility assignment matrix
Create a risk register with mitigation plans
Agree a communication plan and reporting cadence
Kick off the project with the full team
Assign tasks and confirm everyone understands their work
Produce the deliverables to the agreed quality standard
Coordinate vendors, contractors, and dependencies
Keep stakeholders updated against the communication plan
items.note: Consistent updates build trust and prevent surprises.

items.text: Track progress against schedule, scope, and budget
Compare planned versus actual performance regularly
Review and update the risk register at each checkpoint
Run change requests through a formal approval process
items.note: Document every scope change and its impact.

items.text: Adjust the plan and resources when variances appear
Verify quality before accepting any deliverable
Re-check stakeholder needs as the project evolves
Escalate critical issues to the sponsor promptly
Hold regular risk reviews with the core team
Keep a decision log so choices are traceable
Manage expectations on timing and trade-offs
Confirm all deliverables are complete and accepted
Obtain formal sign-off from the sponsor or client
Release resources, contracts, and licenses
Archive documents, data, and final reports
Run a lessons-learned review with the team
items.note: Capture improvements while memories are fresh.

items.text: Hand over to operations and close the project formally

faq.q: What are the five phases of project management?
faq.a: Initiation, planning, execution, monitoring and control, and closing. Each phase has its own goals and deliverables, and this checklist gives you the key tasks for every one.

faq.q: Who is this project management checklist for?
faq.a: Project managers, team leads, and PMO staff who run structured projects. It works whether you follow a waterfall, hybrid, or lightweight agile approach.

faq.q: How is this different from a basic project checklist?
faq.a: It is organized around formal lifecycle phases and adds governance, risk, and control steps. Use it when you need a more methodical, repeatable management process.

faq.q: Does this checklist work with agile projects?
faq.a: Yes. Treat planning and execution as iterative sprints, and use the monitoring section for each review. The closing phase still applies at release or project end.

faq.q: Can I print this project management checklist?
faq.a: Yes. Download the printable PDF, share it with your team, and tick off each control as you complete every phase from initiation to closing.
